messages.subject: Trouble making first shiny app
parts:
So i'm starting with a straightforward app. I work in finance so that is my focus.

Download and plot a graph of a stock.

1. UI <- Two inputs, Date and Ticker
2. Server <- Get the inputs and use Quantmod to download stock quotes from yahoo
3. Plot graph


The thing is, i'm not being able to make the plot of the input ticker.

Working code, only for AAPL (Apple stock ticker):

library(quantmod)
library(shiny)

# Define UI for application 
ui <- fluidPage(
  dateInput(inputId = "Start_Date", label = "Start Date"),
  textInput(inputId = "Ticker", label = "Ticker"),
  plotOutput("graph")
)
  
# Define server logic 
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$graph <- renderPlot({
    getSymbols(toString(input$Ticker), src="yahoo", from = input$Start_Date)
    plot(AAPL)
    })
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)


This input gives me what i want and plots a AAPL stock chart given that i input AAPL on the ticker input and put a date in the past. 


but if i change to plot (input$Ticker) so that it also works for other stocks it does not work and gives a ERROR: need finite 'ylim' values



library(quantmod)
library(shiny)

# Define UI for application

  dateInput(inputId = "Start_Date", label = "Start Date"),

    plot(input$Ticker)
    })
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)


The problem is probably very simple and i'm hooping someone can help me!

Thank you

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Trouble making first shiny app
parts:
The value of input$ticker is just a string. To lookup the variable with that name, you could (but shouldn't) use get(input$Ticker, inherit=TRUE) or .GlobalEnv[[input$Ticker]]. I don't like that because input$Ticker is coming straight from the (potentially malicious) client and could refer to any variable in the global environment (or any active frame in the case of get()). It's hard to imagine how plotting any arbitrary value could be bad in this case but still feels like a bad code smell to trust an input string so much.

Instead, I would call getSymbol with auto.assign=FALSE and pass the return value to plot. Or if you plan to use showSymbols or whatever later on, then make an explicit environment using new.env(parent=emptyenv()) and pass that explicitly to getSymbol and showSymbols.
